title: Francisco Alvarez Exits Rehab Game After Hand Injury
text:

Updated 04:20 AM UTC, Thu August 28, 2025
Francisco Alvarez Exits Rehab Game After Hand Injury
Francisco Alvarez’s return to game action produced further questions about his health. Rehabbing a sprained ligament in his right thumb, Alvarez got drilled by a pitch on his left hand and removed from his start for Triple-A Syracuse on Wednesday. After the Mets beat the Phillies 6-0 at Citi Field to complete a three-game sweep, manager Carlos Mendoza had little information other than Alvarez was receiving evaluation on his left pinky. Alvarez started at catcher and went 1-for-2 before departing the game. He is attempting to play through a sprained ulnar collateral ligament in the right thumb that will eventually need surgery. Francisco Alvarez has left the game for Triple-A Syracuse after being hit on the hand pic.twitter.com/Y53td17K2t — SNY Mets (@SNY_Mets) August 28, 2025 Hand injuries have plagued the 23-year-old Alvarez during his brief career. He opened this season on the IL after undergoing surgery for a broken hamate bone in his left hand. Last season, he missed seven weeks after undergoing surgery for a torn UCL in his left thumb.
